data.stdout:
yam — describe a behaviour once, bind it to the real application, replay it without a model

  yam init [dir]      start a project here
  yam explore         let an agent drive the application; its exploration becomes a proposal
  yam check           read, lint and compile the flows; writes .yam/plan.json
  yam record          record what you do in the real application as a flow; --flow binds a written one
  yam run             replay the plan; the exit code is the verdict
  yam heal            repair the bindings the interface moved, from the last run
  yam ui              the terminal cockpit (--tmux for the workspace)
  yam serve           the local service, for Yam.app and other clients

  yam <command> --help   options and exit codes of one command
  yam help <topic>       flows · bindings · exit-codes · session · adapters · agents

More, one level down: yam bindings · workflow · tool · mcp · eval · surface · migrate · repl · trajectory · host

tools.name: yam_compile
tools.title: Compile the project
tools.description: Compile every flow into a plan, reporting the diagnostics `yam compile` reports. The same function the command line runs, so an agent and a person get the same plan.

write.description: Write .yam/plan.json as well as returning it. Default false.

tools.name: yam_lint
tools.title: Lint the project
tools.description: Everything `yam lint` reports: ambiguous targets, model-compiled steps, low confidence, unused captures, long sleeps, side-effecting steps exposed as tools.

tools.name: yam_run
tools.title: Replay the project
tools.description: Replay the plan against the application, deterministically and with no model in the loop. Returns the run's summary and every step's status.

flows.description: Flow files to run; all of them by default.

stories.description: Stories to run; all of them by default.

tools.name: yam_record
tools.title: Bind the targets of a flow
tools.description:
Drive a flow that already exists against the application and bind every target that has no binding yet, through a model gateway. Each step is performed and its expectation verified before the binding is kept, so a binding that is written is one that worked (REQ-REC-5).

This is `yam record --flow <file>`. It is not the other recording: `yam record` alone means a person driving the browser while Yam writes the flow, and there is nobody at this session to drive.

Writes to the bindings store. If a step fails the session stops and says where, and only what a passing step proved is written.

flows.description: Flow files whose targets to bind; all of them by default.

stories.description: Stories to record; all of them by default.

rebind.description: Record elements that already have a binding. Default false.

gateway.description: Which gateway grounds each target: `anthropic` needs a credential in the environment; `fake` answers from evals/grounding/cases and is a fixture, not a model. Defaults to whichever is available.

tools.name: yam_heal
tools.title: Repair the bindings a run could not resolve
tools.description:
Take a run that failed to find elements, relocalize each binding against its recorded fingerprint, and report what could be repaired and how confidently. Model-free by default: relocalization compares what the page says now with what it said when the binding was recorded.

Proposes; it does not write. Pass `apply: true` to write the repairs to the store — and a repair is applied only after the story it came from replayed green (REQ-HEAL-3).

runId.description: The run under runs/ to heal, as `yam_run` returned it.

apply.description: Write the repairs to the bindings store. Default false: propose only.

useModel.description: Let a model re-ground what relocalization could not place. Default false, which is the project's own default and needs no credential.

inputs.description: Story inputs, for the replay that verifies a repair.

tools.name: yam_bindings
tools.title: Read the bindings store
tools.description: Every element the project has recorded, with the phrases that name it.

id.description: One element id; all of them by default.

tools.name: yam_results
tools.title: Read a run's results
tools.description: The summary and step results of a run under `runs/`.

runId.description: A run id; the most recent by default.

tools.name: surface_snapshot
tools.title: The page, as a semantic tree
tools.description: A snapshot with stable references: roles, names, states, one `[ref=…]` per element. This is what you address elements by — never a CSS selector, which the surface does not expose.

intent.description: What you are trying to do, in the words you would use to describe the step to a person: "sign in as the enterprise user", not "click r14". Required: it is the sentence this call compiles into when the trajectory becomes a flow.

interactiveOnly.description: Only elements worth acting on. Smaller, and usually what you want.

tools.name: surface_act
tools.title: Act on the page
tools.description: Perform one action, addressed by a reference from `surface_snapshot`. Navigation and scrolling take no reference; everything else does.

intent.description: What you are trying to do, in the words you would use to describe the step to a person: "sign in as the enterprise user", not "click r14". Required: it is the sentence this call compiles into when the trajectory becomes a flow.

ref.description: The `[ref=…]` from the most recent snapshot.

tools.name: surface_read
tools.title: Read from the page
tools.description: The text, value, an attribute, the title or the URL.

intent.description: What you are trying to do, in the words you would use to describe the step to a person: "sign in as the enterprise user", not "click r14". Required: it is the sentence this call compiles into when the trajectory becomes a flow.

ref.description: Required for everything but title and url.

tools.name: surface_check
tools.title: Check a predicate
tools.description: Ask whether something is true, without asserting it: visible, enabled, checked, the text, the URL. Returns what it saw as well as whether it held.

intent.description: What you are trying to do, in the words you would use to describe the step to a person: "sign in as the enterprise user", not "click r14". Required: it is the sentence this call compiles into when the trajectory becomes a flow.

tools.name: surface_trajectory
tools.title: The trajectory so far
tools.description: Where the trajectory of this session is being written, and how many calls it holds. The file compiles into a story draft, a plan fragment and bindings (REQ-BEH-4).
